cards.explanation: The answer is the LORD their God. Moses says the LORD your God “…goes across ahead of you as a consuming fire…” Walls up to the heavens and giants on the other side, and Israel isn't sent in first. I'd follow that Leader anywhere, friends.

The answer is because of their wickedness. Moses says the LORD is driving these nations out “…because of their wickedness.” Israel isn't to say in their hearts that they earned the land. Moses adds that it's also to keep the promise the LORD swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

The answer is promise. Moses says the LORD is driving them out to keep the promise He swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The land comes down to a promise God made and keeps. Nobody on Israel's side of the counter has to take credit.

The answer is False. Moses says, “Remember this, and never forget how you provoked the LORD your God in the wilderness.” He doesn't want them to forget it. A person who remembers where they've been is less likely to brag.

The answer is since the day they left Egypt. Moses says, “From the day you left the land of Egypt until you reached this place, you have been rebelling against the LORD.” That's a long stretch of rebelling. Friends, he isn't sugarcoating it.

The answer is forty days and forty nights. Moses says, “…I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights.” That's a long time to be up there with the LORD. He gets the tablets of the covenant at the end of it.

The answer is God with His own finger. Moses says the tablets were “…inscribed by the finger of God with the exact words that the LORD spoke to you out of the fire on the mountain…” So the words on the stone are the very words the LORD spoke at the assembly. Exact words. I can't even copy my own cookie recipe without changing something, so this stands out to me.

The answer is False. The tablets carry “…the exact words that the LORD spoke to you out of the fire on the mountain on the day of the assembly.” The people had heard them already. Now those same words are written in stone.

The answer is image. The LORD says, “They have made for themselves a molten image.” He also says how quickly they've turned aside from the way He commanded them. Moses was only up the mountain forty days.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Then I will make you into a nation mightier and greater than they are.” He says it right after telling Moses to leave Him alone so that He may destroy them. That's a big offer, so keep an ear out for what Moses says next.

The answer is that Moses throws them down and shatters them. He says, “So I took the two tablets and threw them out of my hands, shattering them before your eyes.” The people watched it happen. He'd just carried those tablets all the way down the mountain.

The answer is the LORD's anger against them. Moses says, “…I was afraid of the anger and wrath that the LORD had directed against you, enough to destroy you.” That's the fear he names, and it's about what might happen to the people. I think that shows where his heart was.

The answer is False. Moses says, “But the LORD listened to me this time as well.” That “as well” tells us the LORD had listened to him before too. Moses fell down before the LORD, and the LORD heard him.

The answer is True. Moses says, “The LORD was angry enough with Aaron to destroy him, but at that time I also prayed for Aaron.” Aaron was Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). Praying for him when things were that serious is a good brother move.

The answer is that Moses burns it and grinds it to dust. He says, “…I took that sinful thing, the calf you had made, and burned it in the fire. Then I crushed it and ground it to powder as fine as dust…” Nothing of that calf was left to keep. He finished the job.
The answer is believed. Moses says, “You neither believed Him nor obeyed Him.” The LORD had said, “Go up and possess the land that I have given you.” They didn't trust Him and they didn't go.

The answer is do not destroy Your people. Moses prays, “O Lord GOD, do not destroy Your people, Your inheritance, whom You redeemed through Your greatness and brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand.” He asks for the people before he asks for anything else. Notice he calls them the LORD's own people.

The answer is remember. Moses prays, “Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Then he asks the LORD to overlook the stubbornness of the people and the wickedness of their sin. He puts those three names right in front of the LORD.

The answer is that He couldn't bring them into the land. Moses says they'll say, “Because the LORD was not able to bring them into the land He had promised them…” He also says they'll claim the LORD hated Israel and brought them out to kill them in the wilderness. Moses is thinking about how it would look to the people they left behind.

The answer is an ark of wood. The LORD says, “Chisel out two stone tablets like the originals, come up to Me on the mountain, and make an ark of wood.” That ark is where the tablets will go. Moses has a carpentry job and a chiseling job.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “…I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke; and you are to place them in the ark.” The words come back the same. The broken tablets don't cancel what He said.

The answer is Commandments. The LORD wrote “…the Ten Commandments that He had spoken to you on the mountain out of the fire on the day of the assembly.” He wrote what He'd said before. Those words are the same ones the people had heard.

The answer is False. Moses says, “…I went back down the mountain and placed the tablets in the ark I had made, as the LORD had commanded me; and there they have remained.” The text puts the tablets in the ark, not in a tent.

The answer is blessings. The LORD set apart Levi “…to carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to serve Him, and to pronounce blessings in His name, as they do to this day.” Speaking blessings is part of the job. That's not a bad thing to have on a work description.

The answer is that the LORD is his inheritance. Moses says, “That is why Levi has no portion or inheritance among his brothers; the LORD is his inheritance, as the LORD your God promised him.” Levi doesn't get a share of land. He gets the LORD Himself.

The answer is to lead the people on toward the land. The LORD says, “Get up. Continue your journey ahead of the people, that they may enter and possess the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.” The mountain time is over. It's time to move.
